Should we really have a meson option for a single line of code?  Why not supply this as part of the phosphor-networkd config?

As is, we have a single line of code that doesn't even compile and can never be tested in CI.  This isn't a great situation.
Are you suggesting to use this config file "xyz.openbmc_project.Network.conf.in"

No... that config file is for dbus settings necessary to run phosphor-networkd.

I would think that phosphor-networkd would load a config file when it starts up that would allow you to change configuration settings.  That would be better than a compile option (run-time config vs build-time config).

I need suggestion here, isn't it maintaining a config file for each platfom would be tedious job (I have seen some apllication failed to start if some config file missing or because version is missmatch). I have to make release for more than 5 platforms.

We have lots of applications that have a "per platform config file".  In your case it sounds like all platforms need the _same_ config file, so you can supply it as a single bitbake bbappend triggered off a feature that all your systems share.

Isn't it worse to have code in the repository that doesn't even build and isn't even going to be checked in the entire openbmc organization because you're only using this feature downstream?  At least with a config file we can ensure the code compiles and add a unit test for it.

> I have seen some apllication failed to start if some config file missing

I don't know what your point is.  An application that fails to start due to a config file missing, if that isn't the desired design, is buggy and needs to be fixed.  At least it is complaining loudly by not starting though.

> because version is missmatch

We usually use JSON.  We're just talking about adding a JSON keyword.  This isn't a difficult problem.

Do you think that this is often going to be static for a device / image type, or is this something that people will actively need to modify?  Based on your commit message it sounds static.

What we do in phosphor-pid-control is look in `pwd`, followed by `/var/lib/swampd` followed by `/usr/share/swampd`.  The expectation is that someone building a system with this static config would install a file into /usr/share first, but then /var/lib (or /etc) are available to be modified by a user or dynamically if you also want to support that.
